title: Changing of the focus chain algorithm
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

Closely related to issue #11873

There is a discrepancy in the [focus chain] algorithm between the specification versions before and after the [introduction of navigables](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/6315)

In the [old version, the focus chain][focus chain old] algorithm had the following step:

> 5. If current object is a [Document](https://whatpr.org/html/4731/d89b68a...b47435c/dom.html#document) in a [nested browsing context](https://whatpr.org/html/4731/d89b68a...b47435c/browsers.html#nested-browsing-context), let current object be its [browsing context container](https://whatpr.org/html/4731/d89b68a...b47435c/browsers.html#browsing-context-container), and return to the step labeled loop.

In the new version, the [focus chain] algorithm step is now:
> Otherwise, if currentObject is a [Document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#document) whose [node navigable](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#node-navigable)'s [parent](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#nav-parent) is non-null, then set currentObject to currentObject's [node navigable](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#node-navigable)'s [parent](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#nav-parent).

You can clearly see that the old version took the [browsing context container], which is essentially an element (e.g., an iframe). Because of this, the [focus chain] looked like this: `[input, document, iframe, document]`.

If you look at the new version, it takes the [node navigable]'s [parent], which is not actually an element, but a specific [navigable] object in the navigation model. So, when constructing a [focus chain], we'll get something like: `[input, document, navigable]`.

The problem is that if we encounter a [navigable] when constructing the [focus chain], it causes us to stop constructing the [focus chain] due to the `break` condition. This means that if we have focus inside an iframe, we will never have a document from the [top-level traversable] [navigable] in the [focus chain]; in other words, we will have an incomplete [focus chain].

For example, this note directly implies that the [focus chain] will always include the `Document` of the [top-level traversable]:
> Note: The chain starts with subject and (if subject is or can be the [currently focused area of a top-level traversable](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#currently-focused-area-of-a-top-level-traversable)) continues up the focus hierarchy up to the [Document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#document) of the [top-level traversable](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#top-level-traversable).

The algorithm doesn't actually do this, and this is all due to the step that now preserves the [navigable] instead of the [navigable container] (the behavior compatible with the old specification).

This means that the [focus update steps] algorithm will stop the firing focus events as soon as it encounters an item that is [navigable], since it is the last element in the [focus chain]:
> 4. For each entry entry in new chain, in reverse order, run these substeps:
>     1. If entry is a [focusable area](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#focusable-area), and the [focused area of the document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#focused-area-of-the-document) is not entry:
>           1. Set document's [relevant global object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-relevant-global)'s [navigation API](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#window-navigation-api)'s [focus changed during ongoing navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html#focus-changed-during-ongoing-navigation) to true.
>           2. Designate entry as the [focused area of the document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#focused-area-of-the-document).
>     2. If entry is an element, let focus event target be entry.
>     
>         If entry is a [Document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#document) object, let focus event target be that [Document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#document) object's [relevant global object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#concept-relevant-global).
> 
>        Otherwise, let focus event target be null.
> 
>    3. If entry is the last entry in new chain, and entry is an [Element](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element), and the last entry in old chain is also an [Element](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element), then let related focus target be the last entry in old chain. Otherwise, let related focus target be null.
>    4. If focus event target is not null, [fire a focus event](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#fire-a-focus-event) named [focus](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/indices.html#event-focus) at focus event target, with related focus target as the related target.

But firing events isn't the only problem. If the chain is incomplete, we won't get the `Document` of the [top-level traversable]. This means we won't designate a [focusable area] to each document in the [focus chain]. This will lead to disaster when we need to receive the [focused area of the document] for the desired document.

For example API [DocumentOrShadowRoot](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#documentorshadowroot) [activeElement](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#dom-documentorshadowroot-activeelement):
> 1. Let candidate be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [node document](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document)'s [focused area](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#focused-area-of-the-document)'s [DOM anchor](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#dom-anchor).

Here, the first step takes the [focused area of the document], but if it's not designated using correct [focus chain], we risk getting an incorrect value.

For example, we risk getting the `<body>` element instead of the correct `<iframe>` when focusing, say, an `<input>` located inside an `<iframe>`. Of course, we call `activeElement` on the document containing the `<iframe>`.

---

If you want behavior identical to the old version of the specification but with updated text, then this step:
> Otherwise, if currentObject is a [Document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#document) whose [node navigable](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#node-navigable)'s [parent](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#nav-parent) is non-null, then set currentObject to currentObject's [node navigable](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#node-navigable)'s [parent](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#nav-parent).

should be changed to:

> Otherwise, if currentObject is a [Document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#document) whose [node navigable](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#node-navigable)'s [parent](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#nav-parent) is non-null, then set currentObject to currentObject's [node navigable](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#node-navigable)'s [container](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#nav-container).

And in this case, we'll not only get a correct [focus chain] but also get the elements on which focus events will fire.

What's your opinion? I see that focus works completely differently in different engines, and the specification also has discrepancies between versions. So it would be nice to clarify this detail of the specification.

P.S I spent a couple of days studying Firefox and Chrome's focus behavior. But neither behaves as specified by specification, and this is taking into account the issue I mentioned above.
